candidates.alive_premise: One partner discovers that the other has quietly kept evidence of all the versions of them that never became achievements.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: No Aachu/Zuv lived fact is claimed. Specific abandoned drafts or attempts require creator confirmation before personalization.
candidates.title: The Museum of Almost
candidates.concrete_moment: During a desk clear-out, one partner puts a worn folder in the discard pile. The other retrieves it. Inside are crossed-out applications, rough sketches and unfinished plans from different eras. The owner tries to close it; the keeper arranges the pieces by date. The owner then adds today's unfinished draft instead of throwing it away.
candidates.universal_truth: Being deeply witnessed can mean someone remembers your becoming, not only the version that eventually succeeded.
candidates.audience_mirror: People whose partner knew them through abandoned ambitions, changing identities, awkward beginnings or seasons they dismiss as wasted.
candidates.scroll_stop: A partner urgently rescues the least impressive-looking folder from a discard pile.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: The owner sees embarrassing evidence of things that went nowhere; the partner sees a record of how far one person travelled.
scene_proof: The folder moves from drawer to discard pile and back into the partner's hands.
Distinct unfinished artifacts emerge while the owner's posture changes from dismissal to embarrassment.
The keeper lays the artifacts into a visible chronology without praising or explaining them.
The owner places a current unfinished draft at the end, changing a secret archive into a shared living record.
candidates.relationship_motion: One partner protects the archive; the other initially rejects it, recognizes what has been witnessed, and voluntarily continues the record.
retention_ladder: A familiar decluttering action creates an immediate discard decision.
The unusually quick rescue makes the folder consequential.
The contents overturn the expectation of achievements or romantic keepsakes.
The chronology turns clutter into evidence of becoming.
Adding today's draft proves the discovery changed the owner.
candidates.payoff: The archive gives dignity to the versions of a person that existed before certainty, applause or success.
candidates.dm_send_reason: Send it to the person who saw you before anything worked: you remembered me when I could not see a story yet.
candidates.format_recommendation: Carousel as one continuous drawer-to-folder discovery with escalating artifact reveals and a final physical addition.
candidates.asot_turn: The romantic archive contains no conventional milestones—only unfinished selves one partner considered worth keeping.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: witness + rescued discard + unfinished selves instead of milestones + embarrassment-to-dignity + current draft added
risks: A curated scrapbook treatment would feel manufactured.
Specific documents cannot be attributed to Aachu or Zuv without confirmation.

candidates.alive_premise: A tiny habit travels from one family into another person's hands, then quietly reaches the next generation.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: No Aachu/Zuv lived fact is claimed. The illustrative gesture must be replaced by a real inherited habit before personalization.
candidates.title: The Habit That Changed Address
candidates.concrete_moment: At a family meal, one partner folds a cloth around a hot steel serving bowl in the same distinctive two-corner grip once used by the other partner's parent. The spouse notices before the performer does. A younger relative watches and later copies the same fold while passing the bowl onward.
candidates.universal_truth: Long relationships carry family history through unconscious gestures; love can inherit a habit without erasing where it came from.
candidates.audience_mirror: Anyone who has caught a partner's family phrase, hand movement, hosting ritual or practical habit appearing naturally in their own body.
candidates.scroll_stop: A fast visual match repeats one unmistakable hand-fold across an older parent, a partner and a younger relative.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: The gesture feels automatic and personal, yet it belongs to another home and may continue beyond both people.
scene_proof: An older family member establishes the distinctive fold and safe grip.
At a later meal, the partner repeats the exact hand choreography without noticing.
The spouse recognizes it across the table through a precise eye-line and reaction.
A younger relative copies the fold and passes the bowl onward.
candidates.relationship_motion: A family ritual crosses through the relationship, is recognized by the person whose home it came from, and becomes something the couple transmits.
retention_ladder: Establish a visually specific gesture.
Invite recognition through a match cut in different hands.
Reveal the spouse's personal recognition.
Let a younger observer study the action.
The copied gesture makes time visible.
candidates.payoff: One person's inherited definition of care changes homes and enters somebody else's future.
candidates.dm_send_reason: Send it to the partner whose family habits now live in you: your home lives in my hands too.
candidates.format_recommendation: Short Reel using match cuts and repeated hand choreography, with cross-table recognition as the hinge.
candidates.asot_turn: One culturally grounded household gesture shows time; the couple becomes the bridge through which it changes address.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: inherited habit + exact desi hand choreography + three-generation match + cross-table recognition
risks: The gesture must be distinctive enough to register without explanation.
It could drift into shared-adulthood or broad family-values sentiment.
The illustrative gesture is not couple canon.

candidates.alive_premise: A couple plays a game about who started one ritual, but both sincerely give the other person the credit.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: No Aachu/Zuv lived fact is claimed. The goodbye ritual is illustrative and requires a real equivalent before personalization.
candidates.title: Who Started Us?
candidates.concrete_moment: A couple sits back-to-back for one question: who began waiting and waving until the departing partner turns the corner? Both reveal that they believe the other started it. Alternating recollections show each occupying both roles on different days. A present-day goodbye ends with the ritual happening again.
candidates.universal_truth: The most intimate rituals can become so mutually kept that authorship disappears and both people remember receiving the love first.
candidates.audience_mirror: Couples with a repeated goodbye, arrival, greeting or private ritual that neither can remember inventing.
candidates.scroll_stop: Viewers guess which partner began a visible ritual before two hidden answers are revealed.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: A game designed to identify one originator ends with two incompatible memories that are both emotionally true.
scene_proof: The ritual is shown from a restricted viewpoint, withholding who began it.
Two hidden answer boards create a participation hold.
Both partners reveal the other's identity at the same instant.
Alternating memories place each partner at the window and each walking away.
The present-day ritual proves mutual continuation matters more than authorship.
candidates.relationship_motion: The couple moves from playful disagreement to recognizing that each has alternated between giving and receiving the same gesture.
retention_ladder: Show the ritual without its origin.
Offer a binary guess.
Let each partner privately commit.
Reveal the contradiction.
Replay reversed roles.
Resolve in the present through mutual continuation.
candidates.payoff: Both kept choosing the ritual long enough for it to become theirs.
candidates.dm_send_reason: Send it to the person who shares an authorless ritual with you: I genuinely remember the love starting with you.
candidates.format_recommendation: Short Reel with participation-first guess, simultaneous reveal, alternating POV memories and a present-day repeat.
candidates.asot_turn: The familiar game shell opens into a tender dispute between two valid POVs, resolved through role reversal and mutual authorship.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: binary guess + contradictory reveal + alternating POV memory + reversible ritual + mutual continuation
risks: Without the conflicting reveal it becomes a generic couple quiz.
The goodbye action could drift into quiet-presence territory.
The ritual is not couple canon.

candidates.alive_premise: Two pherans hang side by side; before the couple appears, viewers guess whose is whose from the tiny lives collected in their pockets.
candidates.moment_origin_detail: No Aachu/Zuv lived fact is claimed. Pheran use and pocket contents require creator and cultural confirmation.
candidates.title: The Pheran Pocket Test
candidates.concrete_moment: At a winter entryway, each partner grabs the other's hanging pheran. An unfamiliar object emerging from each pocket stops them. They inspect the inventories, recognize whose garment they hold, exchange them, and restore the displaced objects to the correct pockets.
candidates.universal_truth: Intimacy is knowing a person through the ordinary traces they carry, not only through their face or words.
candidates.audience_mirror: Couples who can identify each other's coat, bag or side of a room from its contents; Kashmiri viewers receive the pheran as lived winter context.
candidates.scroll_stop: A face-hidden guessing game presents two pherans and two pocket inventories before revealing either owner.
candidates.emotional_contradiction: A publicly recognizable garment hides private evidence of who each person is.
scene_proof: Two worn pherans hang with distinct ordinary objects peeking from their pockets.
Two hands select the wrong garments and freeze on discovering unfamiliar objects.
The objects cross the doorway with the exchanged garments.
Both restore one displaced object for the other before wearing the correct pherans.
candidates.relationship_motion: A mistaken grab becomes mutual recognition and a two-way exchange; both partners complete the correction.
retention_ladder: Invite the viewer to match each pocket inventory to its unseen owner.
Reveal both confidently choosing the wrong garment.
Let an object expose each mistake.
Delay faces through the mirrored exchange.
Land on both restoring the other's belongings.
candidates.payoff: Love has learned the shape of each person's ordinary, carried life.
candidates.dm_send_reason: Send it to the person whose jacket, bag or pockets you could identify without seeing them.
candidates.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel as a visual match-and-reveal game.
candidates.asot_turn: The pheran is an inhabited relationship object; pocket archaeology carries cultural specificity and tenderness through equal participation.
candidates.novelty_fingerprint: pheran + face-hidden pocket match + mutual wrong grab + two-way exchange + carried traces
risks: Pheran construction and winter-use details require cultural review.
It can feel tokenizing if treated as costume.
Pocket inventories must not imply undocumented belongings.

excluded_candidates.reason: Collides with the already-owned shared-bit/private-conspiracy lane and uses a dining-table object system that risks another cute prop proof.
Familiar courtesy trope with a thin emotional turn; close to small-care and public-sacrifice content despite mutual staging.
